profile.name: Zhaniya Turganova
profile.mapIntro: Hi — my experiences are multifaceted, so here's a Venn diagram that shows it best. I love intersections. Click any dot for the full story.
profile.bio:
How can I affect as many people with as much positive economic impact in the shortest period of time?

Functional hardware (I like things that do things!) has allowed me to follow this goal in conjunction with what I am good at—sciences, programming, and architecture—which you can just call engineering, but I think the specifics allow for a clearer comprehension of what I do. My mission is to be a world-class general architect of systems, processes, and reactions to make naturally occurring things serve our society.

I find coincidences beautiful—math operations that happen naturally in physics—and if you tell me the answer is (as it always is) actually just zero, I won't hate it!

Look at my profile and tell me where you think we are the same and different. All I do is for a conversation and I am curious of your perspective on things I care and may not care about.

thoughts.title: On Building
thoughts.body: Problems are great because you're forced to solve them, whether there is decades worth of research to rationalise yourself or there's 1 paper written on the topic — and it's yours. I am excited about issues where I have to consider physical interactions and explore novel designs, especially small-scale phenomena about which a PhD will tell you they have no clue (fun fact — we are closer to being the size of the whole universe than the size of a fundamental particle!)

thoughts.title: As we have seen, technological progress is like a pigeon you fed once — the more you give it, the more it wants. We will always be busy with problems of our own doing (did someone say AI?).
What's Next
thoughts.body: My current focus is computing infrastructure for AI. I research novel computing paradigms and would love to see universal shift from Von Neumann computing to — you name it — neuromorphic, in-memory, quantum. I used to be wary and disliking of numbers when I was younger, but turns out it's all just physics, which is, obviously, more likeable.

experiences.title: Ferroelectric Transistors for Compute-in-Memory
experiences.org: Founder & Research Lead · 1517 Fund Flux Capacitor program
bullets: received a $100K investment offer from the 1517 Fund Flux Capacitor program — selected as 1 of 10 funded projects from 300+ applications — to develop an all-van-der-Waals ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) for analog compute-in-memory AI inference

designed an MFIS (metal-ferroelectric-insulator-semiconductor) stack — sapphire (Al₂O₃) substrate for high-quality van der Waals epitaxy, few-layer InSe channel grown by MBE for electron mobility well above silicon, α-In₂Se₃ ferroelectric gate stable at atomic thickness, self-passivating native oxide as the insulating barrier, indium source/drain contacts for low-resistance Ohmic injection

core thesis: a single indium-material-family stack grown in one vacuum cycle eliminates the reactive heterogeneous interfaces and charge-trap states that limit silicon-based FeFETs, while retaining InSe's intrinsic high electron mobility
evaluated SRAM, RRAM, PCM, and HfO₂-on-silicon FeFETs; compared MFIS vs. MFMIS and double-gated architectures to select the prototype path

target metrics: electron mobility ≥200 cm²/V·s (~2× silicon), on/off ratio >10⁴, memory window ≥1 V, retention >10⁴ s, endurance to 10⁵ cycles — followed by a 4×4–8×8 crossbar array demonstrating vector-matrix multiplication

validation plan: in-situ RHEED and post-growth AFM for channel crystal quality, piezoresponse force microscopy for clean polarization switching, full fabrication and electrical characterization across ~10 devices

advised by Dr. Asif Khan (GT ECE/MSE; Editor-in-Chief, IEEE JxCDC) and Prof. Lauren Garten (In₂Se₃ materials expert); authored a technical white paper and a 6-month milestone plan with provisional patent filing

experiences.title: Silicon Jackets — Digital Design · Digital Verification · Physical Design
experiences.org: Physical Design Engineer · Georgia Tech Chip Design Club
bullets: contributed to a student-led team building a custom digital ASIC from scratch — driving the processor pipeline from RTL all the way to a fully verified, manufacturable GDSII layout
designed a 32/64-bit SRAM-backed calculator in SystemVerilog — 7-state FSM controller, parameterized ripple-carry adder, two-stage carry-chained 64-bit addition, dual CF_SRAM_1024x32 hard macros

built a parameterized UVM-style testbench — constrained-random sequences, clocking-block driver, one-cycle read-latency monitor, dual-memory golden-model scoreboard; 98.94% functional coverage and 100% SVA pass rate in Cadence IMC
performed manual STA across all FF-to-FF paths; parsed post-simulation timing reports with Python to extract 50 violated paths and compute the optimal clock frequency (943 MHz)

executed a complete RTL-to-GDS flow in Cadence Genus/Innovus — synthesis, floorplanning, PDN generation, CTS, macro-aware routing, STA in Tempus; ported YAML-abstracted flows to a fully Tcl-driven methodology in Innovus Stylus and benchmarked against OpenLane

diagnosed and resolved 1,000+ DRC violations to zero by tracing root cause to SRAM LEF OBS constraints; fixed via routing-layer expansion, placement halos, and macro routing blockages — timing closure from WNS −2.701 ns to +0.01 ns
experiences.personal: I joined because I wanted to feel a design go all the way from a line of code to silicon. For anyone thinking of joining — absolutely do! It took me a few grey hairs, but the leads are super supportive, and the onboarding program is very well-developed.

experiences.title: UniSAT Nano-Satellite Programme
bullets: Nanosatellite assembly, 3D modeling, PCB design, IoT systems; designed and tested onboard data-collection sensors
experiences.personal: One of my first exposures to aerospace.

experiences.title: HyTech Formula SAE Racing
experiences.org: Electrical Engineer · Georgia Tech's student-run electric race car team
bullets: designed a 2-layer PCB in Altium Designer — created custom schematic symbols and footprints from component datasheets, calculated RC values to meet target frequency and duty-cycle specifications
integrated USB-C power delivery into the board design; performed full trace routing, via placement, copper pour, and complete DRC verification for fabrication readiness

experiences.title: Facchetti Laboratory, Georgia Tech
bullets: fabricate organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) from novel conducting polymers for neuromorphic computing — executing the complete cleanroom flow: photolithographic mask alignment, e-beam gold evaporation of source/drain contacts, spin coating of polymer active layers
electrically characterize devices on a Signatone probe station, extracting transfer curves and transconductance to evaluate electrochemical switching behavior

screen NMOS/PMOS polarity of previously uncharacterized polymers by interpreting I-V curve directionality — determining carrier type, accumulation vs. depletion mode operation, and channel performance for novel materials
document fabrication procedures and measurement protocols for lab repeatability
experiences.personal: The lab culture is great, I enjoyed being taught by my mentors and getting hands on experience with very cool metrology tech and cleanrooms was genuinely so rewarding and taught me a lot of the knowledge I build my current project on.

experiences.title: 2D Heterostructure Synthesis VIP
experiences.org: Undergraduate Researcher · MBE Growth of γ-InSe · Georgia Tech
bullets: performed molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) growth of γ-InSe thin films on sapphire and Si(100) substrates under ultra-high vacuum (UHV)

researched optimization of Se/In flux ratio and substrate temperature to stabilize the target crystal phase — interpreting RHEED, XRD, AFM, SEM, TEM, profilometry, and Hall mobility data to guide growth parameters
applied machine learning to modulate substrate temperature and source flux in real time during growth runs
built an automated mechanical exfoliation and transfer tool to reliably move MBE-grown InSe flakes from sapphire onto silicon — enabling high-mobility 2D channel layers on industry-standard wafers
used profilometry to measure differential film thickness across the wafer; deposited a patterned Georgia Tech logo onto a wafer as a process demonstration
experiences.personal: Once again, loved the people I worked with. Most were incredibly curious physics majors, and I liked the approach of us discussing new papers, findings together. It was a great opportunity to use, once again, very cool tech. I joined it because I wanted to research a frontier material and I plan to continue being in this VIP!

experiences.title: Kacher Laboratory, Georgia Tech
bullets: perform TGA and DSC thermal analysis to characterize phase transformations during hydrogen reduction of iron oxide to steel — tracking mass loss to directly quantify reduction extent — for the ARPA-E-funded ROSIE program on sustainable steel manufacturing
conduct SEM imaging and EDS elemental analysis to evaluate microstructural evolution across reduction stages; run density measurements on stainless steel samples
process stainless steel pellets through full metallographic preparation — casting, heat treatment, sectioning, mounting, grinding, polishing; use ImageJ for grain-size analysis and feature extraction

lead customer discovery and market validation for ROSIE commercialization — ran technical and commercial interviews with engineering teams at NASA and Blue Origin to represent voice-of-customer and surface market requirements
assessed commercialization verticals from hydrogen precooler heat exchangers to semiconductor UHP gas delivery; built an autonomous outreach agent targeting defense, aerospace, and solar PV verticals
experiences.personal: I am incredibly thankful for all the experiences I had in this lab — all our PIs and PhDs took time to mentor a very, at the time, green freshman. The skills I got in this lab are incredibly versatile and I was able to be involved in research both from the science and commercialization perspective.

experiences.title: Materials Innovation & Learning Laboratory, Georgia Tech
bullets: trained on and operated shared characterization instrumentation — Instron and Mark-10 mechanical testers, microhardness tester, DSC, TGA, IR camera, UV-Vis spectrophotometer, and contact angle goniometer
supported sample preparation, instrument maintenance, and user training across the facility

experiences.title: Piper Aircraft
experiences.org: Materials & Process (M&P) Engineering Intern · Vero Beach, FL
bullets: owned a thermoforming defect and yield reduction project end-to-end — independently conceived and designed a full Design of Experiments across a 14-channel thermocouple array, then ran the tests personally and installed the thermocouples myself

researched the plastic deformation and thermal behavior of acrylic-PVC polymer blends — dimensional stability, heat deflection temperature, and structural/phase characteristics that diverge from published neat-material datasheet values

applied statistical process control (ANOVA, Pearson/Spearman correlation, coefficient-of-variation repeatability testing) to isolate the process parameters driving part warpage and distinguish genuine defects from sensor-mounting artifacts

solved a critical instrumentation failure from first principles — derived sheet temperature analytically from thermodynamic heat-transfer equations when the thermocouple repeatedly detached, then remounted the sensor on an insulating layer as a cross-check; both approaches agreed within uncertainty

built custom thermal-mapping software in-house — a Python/SciPy pipeline with automated artifact cleaning and radial basis function (RBF) interpolation over CAD geometry, visualized in PyVista and Three.js/WebGL; also produced a thermal map in Siemens NX
quantified substrate warpage using 3D structured-light scanning (Creaform/VXelements); traced a diagonal warpage signature to a specific thermal imbalance between tool zones
designed an A/B-basis qualification test plan for 4130 steel, statistically establishing material allowables to FAA-regulated standards

audited the aircraft pre-paint surface preparation process to identify the mechanism driving observed corrosion; authored Standard Manufacturing Procedures for alkaline-wash adhesion and aluminum surface preparation
experiences.personal: Incredibly happy to intern there. It was always my dream to work in aviation, because the tech is more exciting than cars, but the timelines aren't stretched out for years like rockets. And the team culture is great as well! So many smart and welcoming people.

experiences.title: Lunar Regolith Geopolymer Concrete
bullets: Optimized NaOH molarity in metakaolin-based geopolymer for lunar ISRU habitat construction; tested setting time and compressive strength
experiences.personal: I loved concrete — because it's so common. My thought was, if I can make new, cheaper, stronger concrete — I could be a billionaire! But, realism — researching concrete for normal daily applications — turned out to be boring. Anytime I feel a research topic is lacking novelty — I just add space to it — and it's exciting, every time. Always been involved with space, and I researched how we can chemically produce concrete from lunar regolith (lunar soil), process it, and build lunar bases! Two years later, I was not surprised to see GRU Space, a lunar regolith moon hotel startup, raise $500k from YCombinator.

experiences.title: Stress Analysis of Dome-Shaped Lunar Bases
bullets: Lagrange-multiplier optimization of hemispherical habitat geometry; Taylor-series tolerance analysis for 3D-printed lunar structures

experiences.title: NASA Johnson Space Center — United Space School
experiences.org: Materials Selection Lead · 1 of 40 Global Delegates · the only person chosen to represent Kazakhstan
bullets: performed materials selection for thermal protection systems on inflatable cargo decelerators and crew landers for a crewed Mars mission design project

researched carbon-carbon composites and refractory alloys for extreme re-entry thermal environments; applied CAD modeling and thermal CFD analysis to simulate aerothermal loads on lander and vehicle structures
evaluated material candidates against mass, thermal conductivity, ablation resistance, and structural integrity constraints
experiences.personal: Probably the most inspiring summer of my life. I met Suni Williams (the astronaut who was stuck on the ISS for 9 months!!) and current Artemis astronaut Luca Parmitano handed me my diploma at our graduation. The hospitality of the NASA community and my host parents, along with the genuine hope and belief the engineers and astronauts have for the future of space exploration, was incredibly inspiring—especially when program funding isn't always certain. Suni Williams told me she hopes us young people stay hopeful and keep dreaming. That has been the driver of my work in uncertain times, whether it's something silly like getting a B on a test, something big like choosing a career trajectory or wondering whether building a hotel on the moon is totally insane or not.

experiences.title: UPenn Jerome Fisher M&T Summer Institute
experiences.org: Software Engineer · 1 of 75 students from 1,000+ applicants · Penn Engineering & the Wharton School
bullets: designed an app for a smart dog collar using Swift; applied unit economics and market sizing to develop a full business plan — recognized as 1 of 5 award winners among 15 teams
participated in a Google IPO simulation at Morgan Stanley NYC; attended lectures taught by Michael Grimes, lead banker on the SpaceX and Tesla IPOs
experiences.personal: First time I experienced the intensity of venture capital, Wall Street, and IB people. M&T took us to the Morgan Stanley headquarters in New York, where the man who led the Google IPO—and recently the SpaceX IPO—Michael Grimes, taught our group of 70 ambitious kids how to run an IPO. That was insane. The knowledge I got from this program, like hearing the word SAFE for the very first time, came full circle when I was offered a $100k SAFE investment myself two years later. I met amazing people who I am still in touch with, whether they're in SF or New York.

experiences.title: AI Chatbots for Space Missions
bullets: 11,000+ word IRB-approved study (8 participants: NASA HI-SEAS + Kazakhstan Space Agency); fine-tuned Alpaca-7B; developed LorelAI social assistant
experiences.personal: My longest-running project. I had the opportunity to research social isolation and actually interview people who participated in a 6-month Mars simulation study in Hawaii. My teammate and I did everything from fine-tuning very early models of Llama (if I played the sound of the AI voice, you would actually laugh), to building a physical robot, testing it, and analyzing every word the interviewees said about our product—and iterating on it, over and over again.

experiences.title: Yale Young Global Scholars — Innovations in Science & Technology
bullets: Designed a research proposal on ALS, studying inhibition of the C9ORF72 gene
Completed advanced seminars and a capstone project with an international team
experiences.personal: The most friends I made and the most fun I had! It was awesome on Yale's campus, spending time in the underground billiard area, discussing topics from philosophy to neuroscience to math, and meeting so many amazing people.

experiences.title: Neuroeconomics in Orbit
bullets: Prospect-Theory analysis of spaceflight-driven neurophysiological changes on astronaut decision-making
experiences.personal: I was excited about neuroscience and space, and this project was the result. I don't tend to trust people's decision-making on Earth—why would I trust them in space? I knew there had to be neurophysiological changes in the brain from all the radiation and gravitational effects, and I wanted to quantify exactly how much their risky behavior could change.

experiences.org: National High School Journal of Science
bullets: 7,500-word paper published in the National High School Journal of Science; mentored by a Georgetown M.D./Ph.D.
experiences.personal: My first deep dive into neuroscience. It was a reeeeeeeeeeeeeeally long paper.
